1	
2	# SiliFuzz - Fuzzing CPUs by proxy
3	
4	## What is SiliFuzz
5	
6	SiliFuzz is a system that finds CPU defects by fuzzing software proxies, like
7	CPU simulators or disassemblers, and then executing the accumulated test inputs
8	(known as the *corpus*) on actual CPUs on a large scale. SiliFuzz is a work in
9	progress, please refer to the
10	[paper](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/master/paper/silifuzz.pdf) for
11	details.
12	
13	## Terminology
14	
15	##### Software fuzzing and coverage
16	
17	Fuzzing is a technique of testing a target (an application, or an API) with a
18	large number of test inputs generated on the fly. The goal is to make these
19	inputs as interesting and as diverse as possible in order to trigger corner
20	cases. In other words, fuzzing aims to maximize the combined code coverage.
21	*Code coverage* may have different meanings, e.g. which basic blocks are
22	executed or which paths are taken in the program.
23	
24	##### Proxy
25	
26	For the purposes of SiliFuzz, a *proxy* is any software or hardware system that
27	behaves similar to some aspects of the target CPU. For example, a CPU emulator
28	or a disassembler. A proxy is needed when we cannot directly collect coverage
29	information from the target.
30	
31	By applying fuzzing techniques to a proxy, we can generate a series of test
32	inputs (corpus) that produce interesting behavior in the proxy. Our underlying
33	assumption is that this translates into similarly interesting behavior in the
34	target. Read more in the [docs](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/main/doc/proxy_architecture.md).
35	
36	##### Corpus / Corpus shard
37	
38	A collection of inputs used for testing the target is known as *corpus*.
39	
40	A reasonably large corpus contains millions of inputs and is usually split into
41	multiple non-overlapping chunks called *shards*.
42	
43	##### Snapshot
44	
45	A SiliFuzz snapshot describes a short sequence of CPU instructions plus an
46	initial state of CPU registers and memory to deterministically execute that
47	sequence. A typical snapshot contains less than 100 bytes of code and runs in
48	microseconds, but it can be arbitrarily large. Snapshots are stored as
49	`silifuzz.proto.Snapshot` protocol buffers.
50	
51	Snapshots are typically created from the inputs generated by a fuzzing engine.
52	For CPU testing purposes these inputs are filtered to eliminate all
53	non-deterministic snapshots. Read more in the
54	[docs](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/main/doc/what_makes_a_good_test.md).
55	
56	###### Expected end state
57	
58	An end state describes the contents of registers and memory expected to exist at
59	the end of a Snapshot execution. If the snapshot executes differently on
60	different CPU microarchitectures it will have multiple expected end states.
61	
62	##### Snap
63	
64	A Snap is an in-memory representation of a **Snapshot** that can be easily
65	loaded and executed by the **Runner**. Snaps are typically loaded from disk by a
66	*reading runner*. The Snap on-disk format is essentially the same as the
67	in-memory one except that native pointers are replaced with offsets. See this
68	[header](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/main/snap/gen/relocatable_snap_generator.h)
69	for details. This format is often referred to as *relocatable*. Each Snap
70	contains exactly one expected end state i.e. Snaps are
71	microarchitecture-specific. Read more in the [docs](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/main/doc/snap.md).
72	
73	##### Runner
74	
75	Runner is a binary for testing a single CPU core. A runner consumes a corpus
76	shard, repeatedly executes random Snaps in it and checks that the expected end
77	state is reached. Runner is a single-threaded process.
78	
79	##### Orchestrator
80	
81	The orchestrator is a process that drives multiple runners. In a typical setting
82	the orchestrator will continuously execute one runner per logical CPU core, and
83	accumulate and report any failures produced by the individual runner processes.
84	
85	## Supported platforms and microarchitectures
86	
87	See [this file](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/main/util/platform.h) for the
88	list of supported microarchitectures.
89	
90	SiliFuzz runs on x86_64 and aarch64 Linux systems. It has been tested with
91	Linux kernel versions 5.x and 6.x. There is no guarantee that it is compatible
92	with older kernel versions. Legacy vsyscall ABI must be turned off to avoid
93	false positives.
94	
95	## Trophies
96	
97	A non-exhaustive list of bugs and defects SiliFuzz has found.
98	
99	### Bugs
100	
101	A logic bug is an invalid CPU behavior inherent to a particular CPU
102	microarchitecture or stepping. SiliFuzz has identified the following bugs:
103	
104	*   [CVE-2021-26339](https://www.amd.com/en/resources/product-security/bulletin/amd-sb-1028.html)
105	*   [Erratum #1386](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/processor-tech-docs/revision-guides/56323-PUB_1_01.pdf)
106	*   [Erratum #1468](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/processor-tech-docs/revision-guides/56323-PUB_1_01.pdf)
107	*   [Erratum #3442699 for ARM Neoverse V2](https://developer.arm.com/documentation/SDEN-2332927/900)
108	*   [Erratum #3213672 for ARM Cortex-X3](https://developer.arm.com/documentation/SDEN-2055130/1400)
109	
110	### Defects
111	
112	An (electrical) defect is an invalid CPU behavior that happens only on one or
113	several chips. SiliFuzz has found the following defects we described in the
114	paper
115	
116	*   F2XM1 Defect.
117	    [Paper](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/master/paper/silifuzz.pdf) /
118	    Appendix A
119	*   Overshoot of an Illegal Instruction.
120	    [Paper](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/master/paper/silifuzz.pdf) /
121	    Appendix B
122	*   FCOS Miscomputes.
123	    [Paper](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/master/paper/silifuzz.pdf) /
124	    Appendix C
125	*   Missing x87 Data Pointer Update.
126	    [Paper](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/master/paper/silifuzz.pdf) /
127	    Appendix D
128	
129	## Related projects
130	
131	*   [Centipede](https://github.com/google/fuzztest/blob/main/centipede/README.md)
132	    is a fuzzing engine developed at Google for fuzzing large and slow targets
133	    like CPU emulators.
134	
135	## Prework
136	
137	### Prework (for Bazel)
138	
139	```shell
140	git clone https://github.com/google/silifuzz.git && cd silifuzz
141	SILIFUZZ_SRC_DIR=`pwd`
142	./install_build_dependencies.sh  # Currently, works for the latest Ubuntu only.
143	bazel build -c opt @silifuzz//tools:{snap_corpus_tool,fuzz_filter_tool,snap_tool,silifuzz_platform_id,simple_fix_tool_main} \
144	     @silifuzz//runner:reading_runner_main_nolibc \
145	     @silifuzz//orchestrator:silifuzz_orchestrator_main
146	SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR=`pwd`/bazel-bin
147	cd "${SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR}"
148	```
149	
150	NOTE: You can use a Docker container to avoid polluting the host system: `docker
151	run -it --tty --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --mount
152	type=bind,source=${SILIFUZZ_SRC_DIR},target=/app ubuntu:noble /bin/bash -c
153	"cd /app && ./install_build_dependencies.sh && bazel build ... && bazel test
154	..."`
155	
156	### Prework (fuzzing Unicorn target)
157	
158	For Bazel, use the following commands.
159	
160	```shell
161	cd "${SILIFUZZ_SRC_DIR}"
162	COV_FLAGS_FILE="$(bazel info output_base)/external/fuzztest+/centipede/clang-flags.txt"
163	bazel build -c opt --copt=-UNDEBUG --dynamic_mode=off \
164	  --per_file_copt=unicorn/.*@$(xargs < "${COV_FLAGS_FILE}" |sed -e 's/,/\\,/g' -e 's/ /,/g') @//proxies:unicorn_x86_64
165	bazel build -c opt @fuzztest//centipede:centipede
166	mkdir -p /tmp/wd
167	
168	# Fuzz the Unicorn proxy under Centipede 1000 times with parallelism of 30.
169	"${SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR}/external/fuzztest+/centipede/centipede" \
170	  --binary="${SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR}/proxies/unicorn_x86_64" \
171	  --workdir=/tmp/wd \
172	  -j=30 --num_runs=1000
173	```
174	
175	NOTE: Please refer to
176	[Centipede](https://github.com/google/fuzztest/blob/main/centipede/README.md#run-centipede-locally-)
177	documentation on how to efficiently run the fuzzing engine.
178	
179	## Tools
180	
181	### silifuzz_platform_id
182	
183	This helper tool is to check that the machine you're running on is supported.
184	
185	```shell
186	$ ${SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR}/tools/silifuzz_platform_id --short
187	```
188	
189	```
190	intel-skylake
191	```
192	
193	NOTE: SiliFuzz CPU detection logic does not account for certain desktop variants
194	of otherwise supported CPUs. The tool will report "Unsupported platform" in such
195	cases.
196	
197	### fuzz_filter_tool
198	
199	The
200	[fuzz_filter_tool](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/main/tools/fuzz_filter_tool.cc)
201	converts raw instructions into Snap-compatible Snapshots. It returns 0 when the
202	conversion is possible and 1 otherwise. This interface is compatible with
203	Centipede
204	[input_filter](https://github.com/google/fuzztest/blob/main/centipede/environment.cc)
205	
206	```
207	fuzz_filter_tool raw_input_sequence
208	```
209	
210	The `raw_input_sequence` file contains raw instructions which will be converted
211	into the Snapshot format using
212	[InstructionsToSnapshot](https://github.com/google/silifuzz/blob/main/common/raw_insns_util.h)
213	
214	Sample usage:
215	
216	```shell
217	# INC EAX
218	echo -en '\xFF\xC0' > /tmp/inc_eax && ./tools/fuzz_filter_tool /tmp/inc_eax
219	echo $?
220	0
221	```
222	
223	### snap_tool
224	
225	`snap_tool` examines and manipulates binary Snapshot protos. It can optionally
226	load raw instructions and convert them to Snapshot.
227	
228	```shell
229	echo -en '\xFF\xC0' > /tmp/inc_eax
230	./tools/snap_tool --raw print /tmp/inc_eax
231	```
232	
233	```
234	Metadata:
235	  Id: inc_eax
236	  Architecture: x86_64 Linux
237	  Completeness: complete
238	Registers:
239	  gregs (non-0 only)
240	    rax = 0x20000000
241	    ....
242	```
243	
244	### simple_fix_tool
245	
246	The simple fix tool takes fuzzing results from Centipede, converts raw
247	instructions into a snapshots with no end states, adds end states to snapshots
248	and finally packages snapshots into a sharded relocatable snap corpus.
249	
250	Currently this runs as a non-restartable process on a single host and everything
251	is put into memory so the size of corpus that can be handled is limited by
252	available memory of the host. Since end states are generated on the host, the
253	resulting corpus is single architecture.
254	
255	### hashtest_generator
256	
257	Experimental: hash tests are randomized structured tests that push entropy into
258	randomly generated instructions and capture the resulting outputs as efficiently
259	as possible. This approach is based on the observation that a non-trivial
260	percentage of defects can be detected by calling the right instruction with the
261	right input. Hash tests aggressively target this simple class of defect to
262	provide an experimental point of comparison for Silifuzz. Currently only x86_64
263	is supported.
264	
265	If you want to generate, for example, 30k hash test snapshots containing
266	instructions supported by Skylake processors in the `/tmp/hashtest` directory,
267	you could run this command.
268	
269	```shell
270	mkdir -p /tmp/hashtest && bazel run -c opt @silifuzz//fuzzer/hashtest:hashtest_generator -- --platform=intel-skylake -n 30000 --outdir /tmp/hashtest
271	```
272	
273	## Frequently asked questions
274	
275	The rest of the document is organized in a How-to manner with each question
276	describing a typical use case. The progression of the questions represents the
277	increasing complexity of the task one is trying to accomplish. Each step
278	typically requires either understanding or the artifacts (sometimes both)
279	obtained at the previous step.
280	
281	NOTE: The document assumes an `x86_64` host/target CPU. The exact output may
282	vary depending on the CPU vendor/stepping/etc and the environment (e.g.
283	Docker/KVM).
284	
285	WARNING: many of the instructions below execute **arbitrary** binary code with
286	the privileges of the running user. The tool does its best to sandbox the code
287	with seccomp(2). Use at your own risk.
288	
289	### How to create a simple snapshot
290	
291	```shell
292	# INC EAX
293	$ echo -en '\xFF\xC0' > /tmp/inc_eax
294	$ ./tools/snap_tool --raw  --out=/tmp/inc_eax.pb make /tmp/inc_eax
295	```
296	
297	```shell
298	# CPUID
299	$ echo -en '\x0F\xA2' > /tmp/cpuid
300	$ ./tools/snap_tool --raw --out=/tmp/cpuid.pb make /tmp/cpuid
301	```
302	
303	```
304	<error log omitted>
305	Could not load snapshot: INTERNAL: Tracing failed: Banned instruction: CPUID
306	```
307	
308	NOTE: To avoid non-deterministic results, various parts of SiliFuzz exclude
309	certain classes of instructions, e.g. CPUID above.
310	
311	### How to inspect a snapshot
312	
313	```shell
314	$ ./tools/snap_tool print /tmp/inc_eax.pb
315	```
316	
317	```
318	Metadata:
319	  Id: inc_eax
320	  Architecture: x86_64 Linux
321	  Completeness: complete
322	Registers:
323	  gregs (non-0 only):
324	    rax = 0x20000000
325	    rip = 0xeb85c12b000
326	    <omitted>
327	End states (1):
328	  Endpoint:
329	    Instruction address: 0xeb85c12b002
330	  Platforms:
331	    intel-skylake
332	  Registers (diff vs snapshot's initial values):
333	    gregs (modified only):
334	      rax = 0x20000001
335	      rip = 0xeb85c12b002
336	      <omitted>
337	```
338	
339	Notice how the end state value of the `RAX` register is `0x20000001`
340	(`0x20000000+1` which is exactly what `INC EAX` does). Also notice that the
341	`RIP` value is the original `+2` which is the size of the `INC EAX` instruction.
342	
343	### How to run a snapshot from a proto
344	
345	```shell
346	$ ./tools/snap_tool play /tmp/inc_eax.pb
347	```
348	
349	```
350	Snapshot played successfully.
351	```
352	
353	### How to convert a single snapshot into a (relocatable) corpus
354	
355	Note: You will need to specify a target platform in order to generate a corpus.
356	In this example, the resulting corpus targets the platform it was generated on.
357	
358	```shell
359	$ cd "${SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR}"
360	$ PLATFORM_ID=$(./tools/silifuzz_platform_id --short)
361	
362	$ ./tools/snap_tool generate_corpus /tmp/inc_eax.pb \
363	--target_platform="${PLATFORM_ID}" > /tmp/inc_eax.corpus
364	
365	# Will play the same "INC EAX" snapshot 1M times
366	$ ./runner/reading_runner_main_nolibc /tmp/inc_eax.corpus
367	```
368	
369	You can inspect the process with gdb:
370	
371	```shell
372	$ gdb ./runner/reading_runner_main_nolibc
373	```
374	
375	```
376	(gdb) b RestoreUContextNoSyscalls
377	(gdb) run /tmp/inc_eax.corpus
378	Starting program: .../reading_runner_main_nolibc /tmp/inc_eax.corpus
379	
380	Breakpoint 1, 0x0000456700010598 in RestoreUContextNoSyscalls ()
381	(gdb) x/i 0xeb85c12b000 # same as the rip value produced by snap_tool print above
382	   0xeb85c12b000:       inc    %eax
383	```
384	
385	### How to create a corpus from an emulator
386	
387	NOTE: This step relies on the "fuzzing Unicorn target" step described earlier.
388	
389	Convert fuzzing result corpus.* into a 10-shard runnable corpus for the current
390	architecture.
391	
392	```shell
393	cd "${SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR}"
394	
395	"${SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR}/tools/simple_fix_tool_main" \
396	  --num_output_shards=10 \
397	  --output_path_prefix=/tmp/wd/runnable-corpus \
398	  --runner="${SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR}/runner/reading_runner_main_nolibc" \
399	  /tmp/wd/corpus.*
400	```
401	
402	The corpus shards will be at /tmp/wd/runnable-corpus.*
403	
404	### How to inspect a corpus file
405	
406	```shell
407	$ ./tools/snap_corpus_tool list_snaps /tmp/inc_eax.corpus
408	...
409	I0000 00:00:1661887744.019079 4074672 snap_corpus_tool.cc:155] inc_eax
410	```
411	
412	NOTE: This is a very basic tool at the moment offering just a few commands.
413	
414	### How to invoke the runner to scan a single core of a CPU
415	
416	```shell
417	# Will play the same "INC EAX" snapshot on CPU#1 10k times.
418	$ ./runner/reading_runner_main_nolibc \
419	    --cpu=1 --num_iterations=10000 /tmp/inc_eax.corpus
420	```
421	
422	### How to scan all cores of a CPU
423	
424	The orchestrator will cycle through all the shards listed in the file passed in
425	`--shard_list_file` argument.
426	
427	```shell
428	$ ls -1 /tmp/wd/runnable-corpus.* > /tmp/wd/shard_list
429	$ echo 'version: "local_corpus"' > /tmp/wd/corpus_metadata
430	# Will repeatedly run the corpus on all available CPU cores for 30s using
431	# /tmp/wd/runnable-corpus.* selected randomly.
432	$ ${SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR}/orchestrator/silifuzz_orchestrator_main --duration=30s \
433	     --runner=${SILIFUZZ_BIN_DIR}/runner/reading_runner_main_nolibc \
434	     --shard_list_file=/tmp/wd/shard_list \
435	     --corpus_metadata_file=/tmp/wd/corpus_metadata
436	```
437	
438	NOTE: The orchestrator can also load XZ-compressed corpus shards from files
439	ending with `.xz`

1	# sdc_pipeline — 可演进 SDC 用例生成闭环框架
2	
3	按 `docs/scheme.md` §4.3/§5 思路构建的五阶段闭环：**Gen → Assess → Filter → Validate → Feedback**，插件化设计（启发式 ↔ RL 可替换），Vault 血缘持久化。
4	
5	## 架构
6	
7	```
8	SeedPool (20 模板 + D13 + evolved)
9	   │
10	   ▼  Mutator 池 (可插拔)
11	   │   OperandBitFlipMutator   — 操作数位翻 (evolution_engine 爬山泛化)
12	   │   OperandDictMutator      — 极端值字典替换 (operand_mutator 体系打通)
13	   │   InsnSequenceMutator     — 指令插入/替换
14	   │   PowerStressMutator      — 功耗应力 Type-I/II (scheme §5.3 雏形)
15	   ▼  Evaluator 池 (可插拔, Unicorn 静态)
16	   │   ACEProxyEvaluator       — 执行中 midflip → diverge 比例 (gem5 注入代理)
17	   │   IBREvaluator            — 逐指令输入位翻转率 (Harpocrates IBR 近似)
18	   │   TogglePowerEvaluator    — 翻转功耗代理 (McPAT 插件位, 见下)
19	   │   AvalancheEvaluator      — 1-bit 扰动雪崩 (反逻辑屏蔽)
20	   ▼  Filter (可插拔)
21	   │   WeightedFilter / ParetoFilter
22	   ▼  Validator (可选重层)
23	   │   Gem5Validator           — golden 自动注册 + CHAOS bit/struct 注入 → 检出率+Wilson CI
24	   ▼  Vault (JSONL)
25	       candidates.jsonl / assessments.jsonl, lineage() 血缘回溯
26	       ↑ Feedback: 高分候选回灌下代种子池; policy 权重自适应
27	```
28	
29	## 快速上手
30	
31	```python
32	from tools.sdc_pipeline.candidate import make_candidate
33	from tools.sdc_pipeline.vault import Vault
34	from tools.sdc_pipeline.pipeline import Pipeline, HillClimbPolicy
35	from tools.sdc_pipeline.mutators import OperandBitFlipMutator, OperandDictMutator
36	from tools.sdc_pipeline.evaluators import ACEProxyEvaluator, IBREvaluator, TogglePowerEvaluator
37	from tools.sdc_pipeline.filters import WeightedFilter
38	
39	seed = make_candidate(open("seeds/e1_carry_chain.S").read(),
40	                      {i: 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0 for i in range(10)},
41	                      [], "seed:e1", structure_tags=["alu", "carry_chain"])
42	pipe = Pipeline(seeds=[seed],
43	                mutators=[OperandBitFlipMutator(3), OperandDictMutator(3)],
44	                evaluators=[ACEProxyEvaluator(n_probes=10), IBREvaluator()],
45	                filt=WeightedFilter({"ace_proxy": 0.7, "ibr": 0.3}),
46	                vault=Vault("output/vault"),
47	                policy=HillClimbPolicy(["operand_bitflip", "operand_dict"]))
48	report = pipe.run(generations=3, per_gen_mutations=3, top_k=4)
49	# 重层 (gem5+CHAOS): validator=Gem5Validator(...), validate_top_k=1
50	```
51	
52	## 演进路线（框架不改，只换插件）
53	
54	| 阶段 | 组件 | 现状 | 演进 |
55	|---|---|---|---|
56	| v1 | HillClimbPolicy | ✅ 三因子启发式 | — |
57	| v1.5 | McPATEvaluator | ✅ 已实装（tsv110 + duty 映射 + peak 功耗） | 时序波形级 duty（需 gem5 stats/PMU） |
58	| v1.6 | EpsilonGreedyBanditPolicy | ✅ RL 第一步实装（ε-greedy 增量 Q） | reward 换 gem5 检出率（E8 证有区分度）→ DQN/PPO |
59	| v2 | AutoµSens | structure_tags 已是雏形 | 接 gem5 结构统计做 STRUCTURE_MAP 逆向靶向 |
60	| v2.5 | 故障模型 | bit + byte_lane_skew + 多bit（gem5 侧） | 时序故障模型 |
61	
62	## 实验记录（框架内）
63	- E7 闭环 vs 随机: 4/60 vs 3/60, TIE（模板 + 注入单位修复实证）
64	- E8 功耗-SDC: A 0% < Type-I 6.7% < Type-II 13.3% 单调（H2 方向一致），统计不足

# sdcfuzz — 面向 ARM64 的 SDC 检测用例生成与跨层验证系统

> Fork of Google [SiliFuzz](https://github.com/google/silifuzz), 原创性重构为**华为鲲鹏 920 (TaiShan V110) 上的静默数据破坏 (Silent Data Corruption, SDC) 定向检测系统**。
> 上游 SiliFuzz 只做"随机 fuzzing → 真机一致性比对"， 本项目在其工程基座之上叠加了**微架构靶向种子、定向变异、gem5-CHAOS 故障注入评分、多板分布式扫描与演化反馈闭环**， 目标是产出高 SDC 检出率的检测用例。

- 完整方案设计： [docs/scheme.md](docs/scheme.md)
- 部署运行手册： [docs/AArch64_Deployment.md](docs/AArch64_Deployment.md)
- 源码级架构合规评估（各组件实现状态）： [docs/experiments/2026-09-03-scheme-compliance-assessment.md](docs/experiments/2026-09-03-scheme-compliance-assessment.md)
- 闭环框架文档： [tools/sdc_pipeline/README.md](tools/sdc_pipeline/README.md)

## 1. 这是什么 / 解决什么问题

数据中心每万台 CPU 中就有几十颗以难以察觉的方式算错 (SDC)。SiliFuzz 的答案是"代理 fuzzing + 大规模真机执行比对"； 但其变异是 operand-blind 的随机翻转， 不针对微架构弱点。本项目 (sdcfuzz) 的核心主张是： **三因子定向生成**——

1. **模板 (骨架)**: 20 个手工微架构靶向种子 (进位链/乘法极端值/电压骤降/LSU 跨界/LSE 跨 die 等， 覆盖 8 个弱点模块)；
2. **操作数空间 (变异)**: 字典笛卡尔积 (确定性， 保覆盖下限) + Centipede 引导探索 (探索式， 提检出上限);
3. **环境应激 (放大)**: 满负载扫描 + stress-ng di/dt 带宽风暴， 逼近真实数据中心工况。

在此之上， `tools/sdc_pipeline/` 把上述流程重构为 **Gen → Assess → Filter → Validate → Feedback 五阶段闭环** (插件化， 启发式 ↔ RL 可替换， Vault 血缘持久化)， 是"持续产出高 SDC 检出率用例"的生成引擎。

**实测效果** (gem5-CHAOS 注入实验， 详细口径见 [docs/experiments](docs/experiments/) 各报告)：
- D13 directed-on-random 变异 vs 纯随机： bit-flip 检出 3.00×, 结构故障检出 7.79× (F4, 500-run); 独立复验 E2 为 3.143× (p=0.00429) / 12.8× (p=5.6e-20), 方向一致。
- 进化引擎 T 因子从 8 演化到 70, SDC 检测提升 8.8× (F5 历史证据)。
- E8 功耗-SDC: A 0% < Type-I 6.7% < Type-II 13.3% 单调 (H2 方向一致， 统计不足， 诚实标注)。
- E7 闭环 vs 纯随机： 4/60 vs 3/60, TIE (模板对操作数变异不敏感 + 注入单位修复后的实测， 揭示了逻辑掩蔽这一真实瓶颈)。

## 2. 系统架构

```
Layer 1 智能生成层        seeds/*.S (20 个微架构模板, // MUT: 可变异槽)
   │                       tools/sdc_mutator/ operand_mutator / csp_targeted_generator / evolution_engine
   │                       tools/sdc_pipeline/ mutators (位翻/字典/指令序列/功耗应力 Type-I/II)
   ▼
Layer 2 故障验证层        Unicorn 静态评估 (ACE 代理 / IBR / 翻转功耗代理 / 雪崩)
   │                       gem5-CHAOS bit/struct/多bit 注入 → 检出率 + Wilson CI
   │                       McPAT (tsv110) 功耗 Evaluator; readset 反逻辑屏蔽
   │                       Vault (JSONL): candidates/assessments + 血缘回溯
   ▼
Layer 3 硬件验证层        snap_tool make → Snap 语料 → Runner (nolibc + seccomp)
   │                       Orchestrator 满核轮转; RunSnapOutcome 2/3/4=SDC, 5/6=噪声
   │                       scripts/distributed_scan.py 3 板 (~446 核) 分布式扫描
   ▼
Layer 4 反馈闭环层        tools/sdc_experiment/feedback.py 三复跑确认 gate → seeds/evolved/ 回灌
                           tools/sdc_pipeline/pipeline.py policy (HillClimb / ε-greedy bandit)
                           → 再变异放大 → 再扫描 (loop)
```

四层的详细设计意图与差距清单见 [docs/scheme.md](docs/scheme.md) §4.3; 每个组件的 file:line 级实现证据见[合规评估报告](docs/experiments/2026-09-03-scheme-compliance-assessment.md)。

### 目录导览 (相对上游新增/重构部分)

| 路径 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `seeds/` | 20 个微架构靶向汇编模板 (E/V/M/C/O/I/L/F 八类) + gem5 probe workload (D5–D13) + 演化产物 |
| `tools/sdc_pipeline/` | **五阶段闭环框架**： candidate/vault/mutators/evaluators/filters/readset/gem5_runner/mcpat_eval + 89 项单测 |
| `tools/sdc_mutator/` | 操作数变异器、CSP 定向生成器、三因子进化引擎、ACE 比例引擎 |
| `tools/sdc_experiment/` | 跨层实验框架： sim_sweep (gem5 注入) / hw_scan / correlation / feedback / devices |
| `scripts/` | 一键脚本 (见 §4) + 分布式扫描 + 板级部署 + D6–D13 sweep 脚本 |
| `gem5_config/` | gem5-CHAOS 注入配置 (two_level_taishan.py: CHAOSReg/CHAOSPhysReg/CHAOSLSQFwd byte_lane_skew) |
| `third_party/mcpat/` | McPAT submodule (Kunpeng920 支持), 配置 `tools/sdc_pipeline/mcpat_configs/tsv110.xml` |
| `docs/scheme.md` | 总体方案 (四层架构 + 三大创新方向 AutoµSens / RL 变异 / 功耗应力分类学) |
| `docs/experiments/` | 每个实验的完整记录 (E1–E8v2, McPAT, 合规评估) |

SiliFuzz 原生管线 (proxies → snapshot → runner → orchestrator) 保持上游结构不变， 详见 [doc](doc/) 与源码各目录; 上游 README 内容已浓缩至 §6。

## 3. 端到端数据流 (一条 Snapshot 的生命)

```
seeds/e1_carry_chain.S  ──as/objcopy──▶  seeds/bin/e1_carry_chain.bin
        │
        ├─ 阶段 A (确定性): operand_mutator 对 // MUT: 槽字典笛卡尔积
        │    → output/variants/*.S → output/bin_stage_a/*.bin
        │    → snap_tool --raw make → .pb → generate_corpus → sdc_stage_a.corpus
        │
        ├─ 阶段 B (探索式): Centipede --corpus_from_files=bin_stage_a/
        │    → /tmp/centipede_wd_guided/corpus.* → simple_fix_tool_main → sdc_stage_b.*
        │
        └─ 合并 shard_list + metadata
             │
             ▼
   reading_runner_main_nolibc (单核, nolibc+seccomp, 无 syscall 执行快照)
             │  orchestrator 每核一 runner, 轮转 shard
             ▼
   mismatch / SNAPSHOT_FAILED → RunSnapOutcome 2/3/4 = SDC 命中
             │
             ▼
   feedback.py: 三复跑确认 gate → 确认者回灌 seeds/evolved/<hash>.bin
             │
             ▼
   再变异放大 (run_guided_mutation.sh) → 再打包 → 再扫描   ⟲ 闭环
```

同一批候选在进入真机前， 可先过 `tools/sdc_pipeline` 的轻量评估 (Unicorn: ACE 代理/IBR/雪崩/翻转功耗) 和重层验证 (gem5 golden 自动注册 + CHAOS 注入检出率)， 只把高检出率候选推上真机。

## 3a. 代码架构 (面向读者/贡献者)

**上游继承的执行基座** (SiliFuzz, x86_64→AArch64 移植)：
- `proxies/` Unicorn CPU 模拟代理 (fuzz 目标)； `fuzzer/` Centipede 集成 + 指令变异器
- `common/` Snapshot proto + raw_insns_util; `snap/` 可重定位 Snap 格式 + 语料工具
- `runner/` 单核播放器 — nolibc, seccomp 沙箱, 汇编 trampoline 换寄存器态, **零 syscall**
- `orchestrator/` 进程调度器； `instruction/` 反汇编与静态指令过滤； `tracing/` 指令级 tracer
- `util/` 平台识别 (PlatformId 是支持微架构的唯一权威), `util/aarch64/` 寄存器保存/恢复 asm

**本项目新增的 SDC 智能层** (按数据流)：
- 生成： `seeds/*.S` 模板 + `tools/sdc_mutator/*` (operand_mutator 字典变异, csp_targeted_generator CSP 定向生成, evolution_engine 三因子爬山)

## 5. 高 SDC 检出率从哪里来 (机理)

1. **定向而非随机**： D13 `pick_high_toggle` (popcount 进位链代理) 的 directed-on-random 相比纯随机 bit-flip 检出提升 3.00×, 结构故障 7.79× (gem5-CHAOS 实测)。
2. **避开逻辑掩蔽**： M2/E7 实证变异目标被"写前不读"覆写则变异无效。`readset.py` 只在指令序列实际消费的寄存器上选变异目标； avalanche 评估器惩罚高掩蔽候选。
3. **功耗应力注入**： Type-I (持续高功耗)/Type-II (高低交替 di/dt) 变异器 + McPAT (tsv110) 功耗评估， E8 实测检出率单调性 A < Type-I < Type-II。
4. **故障注入预验证**： gem5-CHAOS (bit/byte_lane_skew/多bit) 在上真机前量化候选检出率， 只推高检出率候选； fault-clock 取候选自身 ROI [20%,80%]。
5. **真机环境应激**： 满负载 + stress-ng 制造 di/bandwidth 风暴， 逼近数据中心工况； RunSnapOutcome 区分真 SDC (2/3/4) 与噪声 (5/6, 如满负载 fork/mmap 资源耗尽 SIGSEGV)。
6. **闭环持续进化**： policy (HillClimb → ε-greedy bandit) 按上代各变异器表现调权； Vault 血缘可回溯任一候选的演化路径。

## 7. 已知边界与诚实声明

以下是实测发现并如实记录的局限， 不掩饰：
1. **AutoµSens / RL 全流程 / 功耗应力 Type-III**： scheme 的三大创新组件截至 2026-09-03 实现度为 0, 当前只有 ε-greedy bandit (RL 第一步) 与 Type-I/II 变异器雏形。详见[合规评估报告 §7 差距清单](docs/experiments/2026-09-03-scheme-compliance-assessment.md)。
2. **E7 闭环 vs 纯随机 TIE**： 4/60 vs 3/60 — 现有自包含模板对操作数变异不敏感 (LOAD 宏自带常量构造), 需 D13 风格消费初值寄存器的种子或 `// MUT:` 槽改写。
3. **E5 Sim→HW 关联 NOT_SIGNIFICANT**: ρ=-0.2219, p=0.74733, 只有方法学骨架， 无阳性结果。
4. **0201 板不可达**： 实际 3 板可用 (0101/0102/0103), E4 仅单远程板 (0101) 全链路验证； "4 板 446 核" 的历史表述已收敛为 "3 板 ~446 核"。
5. **McPAT 绝对功耗高估**： 最低支持 22nm, 真实 V110 是 7nm; 指标名带 `power_mcpat_w` 且携带 `power_note` 近似声明, 相对比较可信。
6. **短序列 ACE 窗口小**： 5 指令序列 bit×10 注入 diverge=0 (CI 上界 0.28), 需更长序列/更多样本。
7. **满负载 SIGSEGV 噪声**： `--max_cpus=$(nproc)` 满载时偶发 fork/mmap 资源耗尽击中 snap 外路径, orchestrator 容错继续, 按噪声统计不按 SDC 计。
8. **MCE 红线**： 128 核服务器上满核并行构建/fuzzing 会触发内核 Machine Check Exception 物理重启, 所有脚本已内置 `--jobs=32`/`-j=10`/gem5 ≤4 上限。
